MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The USB 3.0 flash drive feels useful because it connects directly to my past USB expansion purchase and offers portable storage for that setup.",
    "The wired headphones with a microphone resemble my previous headset, and the surge protector fits my practical accessory purchases, though I would need a replacement or a specific use before choosing either."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Buying a tablet mount does not mean I need another tablet, and nothing in my history establishes that I own a Kindle compatible with the recommended case.",
    "My networking accessories do not establish a Wi-Fi coverage problem, so the extender lacks a clear purpose for me. The streaming stick and disc sleeves likewise address needs I have not shown.",
    "The AirPods share an audio purpose with my headset, but my history supports a wired microphone accessory; it does not establish a preference for wireless earbuds or ownership of a compatible phone."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My purchases seem to have been treated as broad interest in electronics, when I usually choose accessories for specific practical tasks.",
    "Owning an accessory seems to have been taken as a reason to recommend related devices, even though a mount or adapter can help me keep using equipment I already have."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "Connection types and practical compatibility matter to me: USB 3.0 gives the flash drive a concrete link to my expansion card, while the Kindle case requires ownership that my history does not establish.",
    "My purchases are infrequent and spread across years. A past headset or networking purchase alone gives little reason to assume I need a replacement or upgrade now."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations partly recognized my interest in practical accessories but too often turned that into assumed needs for devices, upgrades, or equipment-specific add-ons."
}
